fasteners.captive_nut_slot.summary: Negative (subtract me) side-entry slot for a captive hex nut plus the screw clearance hole.

params.name: size
params.description: nut size: M2, M2.5, M3, M4, M5

params.name: slot_length
params.description: how far the entry slot runs from the nut centre in +X (reach the part's edge)

params.name: nut_clearance
params.description: added across flats so the nut slides in

params.name: thickness_clearance
params.description: added to nut thickness

params.name: screw_depth_above
params.description: screw clearance hole length in +Z above the nut

params.name: screw_depth_below
params.description: screw clearance hole length in -Z below the nut

params.name: screw_oversize
params.description: FDM oversize on the screw hole

material_notes.orientation: nut axis vertical; if the slot roof is a horizontal bridge keep slot_length short or add a sacrificial layer

fasteners.captive_nut_slot.docstring:
Cutter centred on the nut, nut mid-plane at z=0, slot running in +X.

Example:
    body = body - Pos(x, y, z_nut) * captive_nut_slot("M3", slot_length=wall_to_edge)
fasteners.captive_nut_slot.example: body = body - Pos(x, y, z_nut) * captive_nut_slot("M3", slot_length=wall_to_edge)

fasteners.clearance_hole.summary: Negative (subtract me) clearance hole for a metric screw, with print oversize and optional counterbore or countersink.

params.name: size
params.description: screw size: M2, M2.5, M3, M4, M5

params.name: depth
params.description: hole length along -Z from the surface at z=0 (make it through the whole part)

params.name: fit
params.description: ISO 273 series: fine, medium, coarse

params.name: print_oversize
params.description: added to diameter because FDM holes print small (0.2-0.4 typical)

params.name: head
params.description: none, counterbore (socket head) or countersink (90 deg)

params.name: head_clearance
params.description: added to head diameter for counterbore/countersink

params.name: head_depth
params.description: counterbore depth; default = head height

material_notes.orientation: any; for horizontal holes use primitives.teardrop instead

fasteners.clearance_hole.docstring:
Cutter whose top face sits at z=0 and extends downward ``depth``.

Example:
    plate = plate - [Pos(x, y, plate_t) * clearance_hole("M3", depth=plate_t) for x, y in pts]
fasteners.clearance_hole.example: plate = plate - [Pos(x, y, plate_t) * clearance_hole("M3", depth=plate_t) for x, y in pts]

fasteners.heat_set_boss.summary: Cylindrical boss with a correctly sized pocket for a brass heat-set insert.

params.name: size
params.description: insert size: M2, M2.5, M3, M4, M5

params.name: height
params.description: total boss height from its base (z=0) to the insert face

params.name: wall
params.description: plastic wall around the insert hole; defaults to the insert's minimum

params.name: pocket_depth
params.description: insert pocket depth; default = insert length + 1 mm for melt relief

params.name: top_chamfer
params.description: lead-in chamfer at the mouth of the pocket (helps the insert seat square)

params.name: base_fillet
params.description: fillet where the boss meets its parent surface (0 = none)

params.name: through
params.description: make the pocket a through hole (for bosses on thin floors)

material_notes.orientation: boss axis vertical (insert pressed in along Z); pocket walls are then continuous perimeters
material_notes.notes: Insert pocket is sized per the insert spec, never per the screw. In PLA keep iron at ~200 C.

fasteners.heat_set_boss.docstring:
Boss standing on z=0 with an insert pocket opening at the top.

The boss is centred on the origin so it can be placed with a Location::

Example:
    from lib.component import locations_of
    from lib.patterns.pi import pi5_mount
    bosses = Part() + [loc * heat_set_boss("M2.5", height=6) for loc in locations_of(pi5_mount())]
    floor = floor + bosses
fasteners.heat_set_boss.example:
from lib.component import locations_of
from lib.patterns.pi import pi5_mount
bosses = Part() + [loc * heat_set_boss("M2.5", height=6) for loc in locations_of(pi5_mount())]
floor = floor + bosses

fasteners.heat_set_pocket.summary: Negative (subtract me) pocket for a heat-set insert in a solid wall or floor.

params.name: size
params.description: insert size: M2, M2.5, M3, M4, M5

params.name: depth
params.description: pocket depth; default = insert length + 1 mm

params.name: extra
params.description: extra height above z=0 so the cutter clears the surface cleanly

material_notes.orientation: pocket axis vertical preferred

fasteners.heat_set_pocket.docstring:
Cylinder to subtract; its top face sits at z=0 (the wall surface) and it
extends downward by ``depth``.

Example:
    lid = lid - [loc * heat_set_pocket("M3") for loc in locations_of(holes)]
fasteners.heat_set_pocket.example: lid = lid - [loc * heat_set_pocket("M3") for loc in locations_of(holes)]

fasteners.screw_boss.summary: Boss with a pilot hole for a machine screw to self-thread into printed plastic.

params.name: size
params.description: screw size: M2, M2.5, M3, M4, M5

params.name: height
params.description: boss height from z=0

params.name: wall
params.description: wall around the pilot (>= 2 perimeters, 1.6 mm recommended for M3)

params.name: pilot_d
params.description: pilot hole diameter; default from hardware table (thread-forming size)

params.name: pilot_depth
params.description: pilot depth; default = full height minus one wall thickness of floor

params.name: top_chamfer
params.description: entry chamfer

params.name: base_fillet
params.description: fillet at the base (0 = none)

material_notes.orientation: boss axis vertical so the screw threads cut across layers, not between them
material_notes.notes: Good for ~5 insert/remove cycles. Use heat_set_boss for anything serviced often. PLA cracks under over-torque.

fasteners.screw_boss.docstring:
Boss standing on z=0, pilot hole opening at the top.

Example:
    boss = screw_boss("M3", height=10)
    body = body + Pos(20, 10, floor_t) * boss
fasteners.screw_boss.example:
boss = screw_boss("M3", height=10)
body = body + Pos(20, 10, floor_t) * boss

mechanisms.cantilever_latch.summary: Cantilever snap-fit hook: flexing beam along +Z from z=0 with a ramped hook on the +X face at the tip.

params.name: length
params.description: beam length from root (z=0) to the underside of the hook

params.name: width
params.description: beam width (Y)

params.name: thickness
params.description: beam thickness (X) — the flexing dimension

params.name: hook_depth
params.description: how far the hook protrudes in +X beyond the beam face = deflection required to release

params.name: hook_height
params.description: height of the hook block (Z)

params.name: entry_angle
params.description: ramp angle on the top of the hook (lower = easier to push closed)

params.name: retention_angle
params.description: angle of the underside of the hook (90 = permanent, 45 = easy release)

params.name: root_fillet
params.description: fillet at the beam root to spread stress

material_notes.orientation: beam lying flat in the bed plane (beam length along X or Y, thickness along Z). Never print the beam standing up: bending then peels layers apart and the root cracks.
material_notes.notes: PETG and ABS/ASA flex reliably; PLA snaps below ~1.2 mm thickness or after a few dozen cycles. Strain at the root ~ 1.5*t*hook_depth/length^2 — keep under ~2% for PETG. Defaults give ~1.0%.

mechanisms.cantilever_latch.docstring:
The beam's back face is at x=0 (attach it there), hook faces +X.
Total height = length + hook_height.

Example:
    latch = cantilever_latch(length=10, thickness=1.6)
    lid = lid + Pos(x, y, lid_t) * Rot(0, 0, 180) * latch     # hook facing inward
    body = body - Pos(x, y, z) * latch_window(width=6, hook_depth=1.2)
mechanisms.cantilever_latch.example:
latch = cantilever_latch(length=10, thickness=1.6)
lid = lid + Pos(x, y, lid_t) * Rot(0, 0, 180) * latch     # hook facing inward
body = body - Pos(x, y, z) * latch_window(width=6, hook_depth=1.2)

mechanisms.latch_window.summary: Negative (subtract me) rectangular window through a wall for a cantilever_latch hook to snap into.

params.name: width
params.description: latch beam width

params.name: hook_depth
params.description: latch hook_depth

params.name: hook_height
params.description: latch hook_height

params.name: clearance
params.description: added around the hook (0.3 slip fit)

params.name: wall_t
params.description: wall thickness to punch through (window depth in X, both ways)

material_notes.orientation: beam lying flat in the bed plane (beam length along X or Y, thickness along Z). Never print the beam standing up: bending then peels layers apart and the root cracks.
material_notes.notes: PETG and ABS/ASA flex reliably; PLA snaps below ~1.2 mm thickness or after a few dozen cycles. Strain at the root ~ 1.5*t*hook_depth/length^2 — keep under ~2% for PETG. Defaults give ~1.0%.

mechanisms.latch_window.docstring:
Window centred on the origin in Y and Z, cutting through X in both directions.

Example:
    body = body - Pos(wall_x, y, z_hook) * latch_window(6, 1.2, 2.5)
mechanisms.latch_window.example: body = body - Pos(wall_x, y, z_hook) * latch_window(6, 1.2, 2.5)

mechanisms.living_hinge_lattice.summary: Lattice (kerf-style) living hinge: staggered slots cut through a panel so it can bend about the Y axis; returns the slot pattern to subtract.

params.name: length
params.description: bend region length along X (direction of bending)

params.name: width
params.description: panel width along the hinge axis (Y)

params.name: slot_w
params.description: slot width (X)

params.name: slot_gap
params.description: gap between consecutive slots along Y in the same column (the torsion links)

params.name: column_pitch
params.description: X pitch between slot columns

params.name: link_w
params.description: solid material between slots in Y = torsion link width

material_notes.orientation: flat on the bed; slot walls vertical. Works even in PLA because links twist rather than bend across layers.
material_notes.notes: Bend radius ~ length / total bend angle; more columns = gentler bend.

mechanisms.living_hinge_lattice.docstring:
Slots alternate offset by half a period between columns. Subtract (extruded through the panel) from your plate.

Example:
    plate = plate - extrude(living_hinge_lattice(20, 40), amount=plate_t)

mechanisms.living_hinge_web.summary: Thin flexible web joining two thicker panels (single-strip living hinge), hinge axis along Y, printed flat.

params.name: width
params.description: hinge width along the axis (Y)

params.name: web_thickness
params.description: flexing web thickness (1-2 layers: 0.4-0.6)

params.name: web_length
params.description: web span between the panels (X)

params.name: panel_t
params.description: thickness of the joined panels

params.name: panel_len
params.description: length of each stub panel included (X) — union your real panels onto these

params.name: fillet_r
params.description: fillet where the web meets the panels (spreads strain)

material_notes.orientation: flat on the bed, hinge axis in the bed plane; the web is then 1-2 continuous layers with extrusion lines along the axis
material_notes.notes: PLA fatigue-cracks within tens of cycles; PP and TPU are best. Fold immediately after printing while warm for PETG.

mechanisms.living_hinge_web.docstring:
Web sits at the bottom (z=0 to web_thickness), centred at x=0; panels extend to +/-X.

Example:
    hinge = living_hinge_web(width=40, web_thickness=0.5)
    part = left_panel + hinge + right_panel
mechanisms.living_hinge_web.example:
hinge = living_hinge_web(width=40, web_thickness=0.5)
part = left_panel + hinge + right_panel

mechanisms.parallel_flexure.summary: Parallel-beam flexure stage: fixed block and moving block joined by N thin beams; moving block translates in Y.

params.name: beam_length
params.description: beam span along X between the blocks

params.name: beam_thickness
params.description: beam thickness (Y) — flexing dimension, 0.8-1.2

params.name: beam_count
params.description: number of parallel beams (2 = classic parallelogram)

params.name: beam_spacing
params.description: Y pitch between beams

params.name: depth
params.description: part depth (Z), i.e. beam height

params.name: block_w
params.description: X width of the two end blocks

material_notes.orientation: flat on the bed with beams in the XY plane so bending stress runs along the extrusion lines, not across layers
material_notes.notes: Stiffness ~ N*E*depth*t^3/L^3. Halve thickness for 8x softer. PLA works for tiny strokes only.

mechanisms.parallel_flexure.docstring:
Fixed block at -X, moving block at +X; whole thing stands on z=0 and is centred in Y.

Example:
    stage = parallel_flexure(beam_length=25, beam_thickness=0.8)
    button = stage + Pos(x_moving_block, 0, 0) * button_cap
mechanisms.parallel_flexure.example:
stage = parallel_flexure(beam_length=25, beam_thickness=0.8)
button = stage + Pos(x_moving_block, 0, 0) * button_cap

mechanisms.snap_groove.summary: Negative (subtract me) half-round groove matching snap_ridge, cut into a wall face at y=0 going into -Y.

params.name: length
params.description: groove length along X

params.name: r
params.description: matching ridge radius

params.name: clearance
params.description: added to radius so the bead seats without binding

mechanisms.snap_groove.docstring:

mechanisms.snap_groove.example: body = body - Pos(0, inner_wall_y, z) * snap_groove(length=lip_len, r=0.6)

mechanisms.snap_ridge.summary: Half-round snap ridge (bead) running along X, protruding in +Y from a wall face at y=0; sits on a lid lip.

params.name: length
params.description: ridge length along X

params.name: r
params.description: bead radius (protrusion)

params.name: end_taper
params.description: reserved (0)

material_notes.orientation: ridge running horizontally along a vertical wall prints fine (the half-round is a shallow overhang)
material_notes.notes: Interference 0.4-0.6 mm total for PETG walls 1.2-1.6 thick; PLA prefers <=0.4.

mechanisms.snap_ridge.docstring:
Example:
lip = lip + Pos(0, lip_face_y, z) * snap_ridge(length=lip_len - 4, r=0.6)
mechanisms.snap_ridge.example: lip = lip + Pos(0, lip_face_y, z) * snap_ridge(length=lip_len - 4, r=0.6)

patterns.corner_holes.summary: Four holes inset from the corners of a length x width rectangle (lid screws / corner bosses), centred on the origin.

params.name: length
params.description: rectangle X (usually the box INNER length)

params.name: width
params.description: rectangle Y (usually the box INNER width)

params.name: inset
params.description: hole centre distance from each of the two adjacent rectangle edges

params.name: hole_d
params.description: hole diameter before print compensation (default M3 medium clearance 3.4)

params.name: print_oversize
params.description: added to diameter because FDM holes print small

material_notes.orientation: any (2D pattern)

patterns.corner_holes.docstring:
Four circles at ``(+/-(length/2 - inset), +/-(width/2 - inset))``.

Pass the box *inner* cavity size and the boss inset to get the corner-boss
centres of a ``rounded_box``; ``locations_of()`` turns them into boss
placements, and the same call with the lid gives the matching screw holes.

Example:
    holes = corner_holes(inner_l, inner_w, inset=3.4)
    bosses = [loc * heat_set_boss("M3", height=h) for loc in locations_of(holes)]
patterns.corner_holes.example:
holes = corner_holes(inner_l, inner_w, inset=3.4)
bosses = [loc * heat_set_boss("M3", height=h) for loc in locations_of(holes)]

Profile drawn in XY: rail lips at y=0 (top, where a clip hooks), base at y=-depth.
Extrude along Z for the rail length.

Example:

Identical spacing to the Pi 5; kept as its own id so models document which board they target.

Example:

patterns.pi5_mount.summary: Raspberry Pi 5 four-hole mount pattern (58 x 49 mm, M2.5) centred on the origin.

params.name: hole_d
params.description: hole diameter before print compensation; default = M2.5 clearance (2.7)

params.name: print_oversize
params.description: added to diameter because FDM holes print small

params.name: active_cooler_holes
params.description: also cut the two 3 mm Active Cooler push-pin holes

material_notes.orientation: any (2D pattern)

patterns.pi5_mount.docstring:
Four circles at the Pi 5 hole positions; subtract from a floor, or use
``locations_of()`` to place bosses.  ``active_cooler_holes`` adds the two
3 mm push-pin holes of the official Active Cooler (x=+29, y=+/-18.5).

Example:
    floor = Rectangle(95, 66) - pi5_mount()
    bosses = [loc * heat_set_boss("M2.5") for loc in locations_of(pi5_mount())]
patterns.pi5_mount.example:

bosses = [loc * heat_set_boss("M2.5") for loc in locations_of(pi5_mount())]

patterns.pi5_port_cutouts.summary: Raspberry Pi 5 connector windows for one board edge as a wall-plane sketch (x along the edge, y = height above PCB top).

params.name: edge
params.description: power (-Y: USB-C + 2x micro-HDMI), usb (+X: Ethernet + 2x USB-A), sd (-X: microSD window)

params.name: clearance
params.description: added on every side of the connector/plug envelope

params.name: plug_envelope
params.description: size windows for the mating plug overmold (True) or just the connector body (False, flush panels)

params.name: ports
params.description: optional subset of port names to include, e.g. ['usb_c']; default = every port on that edge

material_notes.orientation: windows cut through a vertical wall; the wall above each window is a short bridge (<= 18 mm)
material_notes.notes: UNVALIDATED: positions from the official drawing, connector/plug envelopes from Pi 4 data and typical cables — test-fit before printing many.

patterns.pi5_port_cutouts.docstring:
Rectangles to subtract from an enclosure wall so the Pi 5 connectors are reachable.

Sketch frame: x runs along the board edge in hole-pattern coordinates
(lib X for ``power``, lib Y for ``usb``/``sd``), y is height above the PCB
top surface.  Place it with ``Pos(x_of_pi_origin, z_of_pcb_top)`` on the
wall plane and extrude through the wall with ``both=True``.

Example:
    win = pi5_port_cutouts("power")
    body = body - extrude(Plane.XZ.offset(outer_w / 2) * Pos(pi_x, pcb_top_z) * win, amount=wall, both=True)
patterns.pi5_port_cutouts.example:
win = pi5_port_cutouts("power")
body = body - extrude(Plane.XZ.offset(outer_w / 2) * Pos(pi_x, pcb_top_z) * win, amount=wall, both=True)

primitives.box_lid.summary: Flat lid for rounded_box with an inner lip that drops inside the walls; printed upside down (top face on the bed).

params.name: length
params.description: outer X of the box it fits

params.name: width
params.description: outer Y of the box it fits

params.name: wall
params.description: box wall thickness

params.name: corner_r
params.description: box outer corner radius

params.name: thickness
params.description: lid plate thickness

params.name: lip_height
params.description: how far the lip drops into the box

params.name: lip_thickness
params.description: lip wall thickness

params.name: clearance
params.description: gap per side between lip and box inner wall (slip fit 0.2-0.3)

params.name: top_chamfer
params.description: chamfer on the outer top edge (bed-contact edge when printed inverted)

params.name: lip_cutouts
params.description: optional sketch in the lid XY frame subtracted from the lip only (e.g. circles clearing corner bosses); None = full lip

material_notes.orientation: top face down on the bed, lip pointing up

primitives.box_lid.docstring:
Lid plate spans z in [0, thickness] with the lip hanging below z=0 (as
assembled on the box); flip for printing.  ``lip_cutouts`` (v1.1.0) is
subtracted from the lip ring before extruding so the lip can step around
corner bosses that run up to the box rim; the plate is untouched.

Example:
    lid = box_lid(110, 80, wall=2.0)
    lid = box_lid(110, 80, lip_cutouts=Sketch() + [loc * Circle(boss_r + 0.3) for loc in boss_locs])
primitives.box_lid.example:
lid = box_lid(110, 80, wall=2.0)
lid = box_lid(110, 80, lip_cutouts=Sketch() + [loc * Circle(boss_r + 0.3) for loc in boss_locs])

primitives.cable_grommet.docstring:

primitives.cable_grommet.example: back = back - extrude(Plane.XZ * Pos(0, 10) * cable_grommet(4.0, slit_w=2.0, slit_len=12), amount=wall, both=True)

primitives.foot.docstring:

body = body + [loc * foot() for loc in GridLocations(80, 50, 2, 2)]
primitives.foot.example: body = body + [loc * foot() for loc in GridLocations(80, 50, 2, 2)]

primitives.pcb_slot_cradle.summary: Pair of rails with slots that grip a PCB by its two long edges (for boards with no mount holes), centred on the origin.

params.name: board_l
params.description: PCB length along the rails (X)

params.name: board_w
params.description: PCB width across the rails (Y)

params.name: pcb_t
params.description: PCB thickness

params.name: rail_h
params.description: total rail height

params.name: rail_t
params.description: rail wall thickness outside the slot

params.name: slot_depth
params.description: how far the slot bites in over each edge

params.name: clearance
params.description: added to pcb_t (slot height) and to board_w (slot span)

params.name: slot_z
params.description: height of the slot floor above z=0

material_notes.orientation: rails vertical; slot faces are then vertical walls, no bridging
material_notes.notes: Board slides in from the +X end; leave that end open in the enclosure or make one rail cantilevered.

primitives.pcb_slot_cradle.docstring:
Example:
cradle = pcb_slot_cradle(*esp32_dims)
body = body + Pos(0, 0, floor_t) * cradle
primitives.pcb_slot_cradle.example:
cradle = pcb_slot_cradle(*esp32_dims)
body = body + Pos(0, 0, floor_t) * cradle

primitives.rounded_box.summary: Open-top rounded rectangular shell (enclosure body) with floor, standing on z=0; outer dimensions given.

params.name: length
params.description: outer X

params.name: width
params.description: outer Y

params.name: height
params.description: outer Z including floor

params.name: wall
params.description: side wall thickness (multiple of 0.4)

params.name: floor_t
params.description: floor thickness; default = wall

params.name: corner_r
params.description: outer vertical corner radius

params.name: bottom_chamfer
params.description: chamfer on the bed-contact edge (elephant foot)

params.name: inner_fillet
params.description: fillet where floor meets the inner walls (0 = none)

material_notes.orientation: floor on the bed, open top up

primitives.rounded_box.docstring:
Example:
body = rounded_box(110, 80, 35, wall=2.0)
body = body + Pos(0, 0, floor_t) * bosses
primitives.rounded_box.example:
body = rounded_box(110, 80, 35, wall=2.0)
body = body + Pos(0, 0, floor_t) * bosses

primitives.rubber_foot_recess.summary: Negative (subtract me) shallow recess to locate a stick-on rubber foot; top face at z=0, extends down.

params.name: d
params.description: rubber foot diameter

params.name: depth
params.description: recess depth

params.name: clearance
params.description: added to diameter

material_notes.orientation: any

primitives.rubber_foot_recess.docstring:
Example:
body = body - [loc * rubber_foot_recess(10) for loc in GridLocations(80, 50, 2, 2)]
primitives.rubber_foot_recess.example: body = body - [loc * rubber_foot_recess(10) for loc in GridLocations(80, 50, 2, 2)]

primitives.teardrop.summary: Teardrop hole profile (circle with a pointed top) so a horizontal-axis hole bridges without support; subtract from a vertical wall.

params.name: d
params.description: nominal hole diameter

params.name: angle
params.description: half-angle of the point (45 = printable without support)

params.name: print_oversize
params.description: FDM oversize

material_notes.orientation: hole axis horizontal, point up (+Y in the sketch)

primitives.teardrop.docstring:
Drawn in XY with the point in +Y; map onto the wall plane (e.g. Plane.XZ) so +Y becomes up.

Example:
    wall = wall - extrude(Plane.XZ * Pos(x, z) * teardrop(cable_d), amount=wall_t, both=True)
primitives.teardrop.example: wall = wall - extrude(Plane.XZ * Pos(x, z) * teardrop(cable_d), amount=wall_t, both=True)

primitives.vent_slots.summary: Grid of rounded ventilation slots filling a rectangular area, centred on the origin (subtract from a wall).

params.name: area_l
params.description: length of the vented area along the slots

params.name: area_w
params.description: width across the slots

params.name: slot_w
params.description: slot width (>= 1.5 for reliable bridging / cleaning)

params.name: pitch
params.description: centre-to-centre across slots (web = pitch - slot_w, keep >= 1.2)

params.name: slot_l
params.description: slot length; default fills area_l

params.name: rows
params.description: number of slot columns along the length; default 1

params.name: rotation
params.description: rotate the whole pattern in-plane

material_notes.orientation: on a vertical wall run slots vertically so they need no bridging

primitives.vent_slots.docstring:
Example:
side = side - extrude(Plane.XZ * vent_slots(40, 16), amount=wall, both=True)
primitives.vent_slots.example: side = side - extrude(Plane.XZ * vent_slots(40, 16), amount=wall, both=True)
